Q1 FY2027 Tanshin BS, 関税引当金 13,836 at 30 Jun 2026. Accrued, contested; treated as a cash claim on equity rather than an operating cost in the forward flows.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (FY2021 643,736 -> FY2026 1,182,358), rounded; used as the forward proxy because the equity CAGR (28%) is inflated by peak-cycle retention and the EPS CAGR by a near-zero FY2021 base
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3y/5y CAGR (27.5%/28.0%) diverges >30% from revenue CAGR (13.6%/12.9%): the FY2024-FY2026 profit surge is retained earnings on a margin spike, not a volume trend. EPS 5y CAGR undefined (FY2021 EPS -3.25). FCF CAGRs on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less interest income; dividend income not separately available before FY2026): 3y 29.4% (42,036 -> 91,151), 5y 15.9% (43,650 -> 91,151).
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF history: FY2021 43,650, FY2022 24,297, FY2023 42,036, FY2024 72,850, FY2025 85,241, FY2026 91,151 (reported FCF less interest income). SBC is nil throughout so the reported and owner series differ only by interest income. Reported FCF has lagged profit because working capital absorbs ~20-25% of each year's revenue increase (FY2026: NI 157bn + D&A 25bn vs OCF 133bn).

scenario_narratives.base: Fujikura delivers close to its thrice-raised FY2027 guidance (revenue ~1.7tn, OP ~400bn+) and keeps growing modestly into FY2028 on the data-center optical-component pipeline, but the consolidated margin mean-reverts from ~26% to ~16.5% over five years as the industry's simultaneous capacity build (Fujikura 3x, Corning, YOFC, Sumitomo) ends the fiber shortage and pricing power. Revenue plateaus in a FY2030-31 digestion phase, then grows at ~3%. The axes are (1) Telecom segment margin: 37% peak vs ~20% normal, (2) hyperscaler capex durability vs digestion, (3) capex intensity of the 300bn plan vs its returns, and (4) tariff/FX leakage on the US-heavy sales mix.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI/data-center fiber demand proves structural rather than cyclical: Fujikura's capacity expansion sells out as it comes online, the US subsidiary insulates it from tariffs, components and engineering (less fiber-draw-constrained) keep the mix rich, and management keeps under-forecasting. Margins stay mid-20s for three years and settle at 20%, revenue compounds to ~3.5x FY2026 by FY2036.
scenario_narratives.bear: A hyperscaler capex pause coincides with the industry's capacity additions; fiber pricing collapses, revenue retraces to the FY2026 level by FY2029 and margins return to the pre-boom 11-12% EBITDA range. Part of the 300bn expansion is stranded. Net cash and the equity ratio mean there is no solvency question, so this is a valuation bust, not a going-concern one; the terminal value is positive and well above zero.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the business on mid-cycle owner cash flow, not on peak guidance. Fujikura's FY2027 is a genuine step-change in scale, so even the base case capitalises a revenue base ~1.9x FY2026, but the ~26% consolidated EBITDA margin is treated as a shortage rent that normalises as capacity arrives. House and street bases coincide (no SBC). The 15x terminal cap and a 9% JPY WACC are the cyclical-industrial settings; risk is priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin durability: each 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is worth roughly 5% of the base-case value; if the ~26% guided margin proves structural the bull case understates value.
Hyperscaler capex cycle: a 2027-28 digestion phase is the bear path and is weighted 25%, not treated as a tail.
Capex plan execution: up to 300bn Japan+US; stranded-capacity or cost-overrun risk is modelled through capex intensity and the bear margin path.
US trade policy: Section 301 tariffs and the contested 13.8bn CBP provision (deducted in the bridge); an adverse ruling with retrospective duties would be an additional cash claim.
FX: ~2.7bn OP per 1 yen move in USD/JPY; guidance assumes 160.
Timing: the Q2 FY2027 print (early Nov 2026) post-dates the folder's latest filing; a guidance change there moves Y1 directly.

inputs.sbc_source: unavailable-by-design: Japanese GAAP filer; the FY2026 yuho cash-flow statement carries no share-based payment add-back and the company has no material stock-compensation plan (SBC-zero market, owner-fcf-adaptations (e)). SBC rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.fy0_note: CSV/core_metrics label convention: FY2026 = fiscal year ended 31 March 2026 (the company and the Analysis JSON call this 'FY2025'). Year 1 of the projection is the year ending 31 March 2027, the year the FY1,755bn / OP432bn guidance refers to.
inputs.share_count_basis: Post 6-for-1 split (effective 1 April 2026). Issued 1,775,180,526 less treasury 119,020,114 at 30 June 2026 (Q1 FY2027 Tanshin) = 1,656.2m. No convertibles or dilutive instruments disclosed; held FLAT (SBC-zero, no buyback programme since FY2020).
inputs.net_debt_note: Borrowings at 30 June 2026 (Q1 FY2027 Tanshin): short-term 45,694 + commercial paper 20,000 + current bonds 10,000 + bonds 10,000 + long-term borrowings 30,250 = 115,944; plus lease liabilities 16,636 (31 March 2026 yuho; not broken out in the quarterly BS) = 132,580. Cash and deposits 192,323. Net cash 59,743 (presentation's own 'net cash' was 96.2bn at Mar-2026 ex leases; the Q1 drop is working capital build and the year-end dividend).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A) leases as debt: lease liabilities (16,636) are in total_debt; lease principal repayments (2,042 in FY2026) are NOT deducted from the flows; ROU depreciation sits inside D&A. J-GAAP filer: operating leases are already expensed inside EBITDA.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows: non-controlling interests take ~2.6% of EBIT (FY2026 NCI profit 4,885 on OP 188,707), folded into cash_tax_rate_path as ~2.5pp of leakage on top of a ~28% cash tax rate. NCI book (32,980 at Jun-2026) is therefore NOT deducted in the bridge.
inputs.interest_income_note: Stripped 2,699 = interest received 1,841 + dividends received 858 (FY2026 yuho P&L). The matching assets (cash 192,323 in net debt; investment securities 56,052 in the equity bridge) are added once, so the income leaves the flows once.
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-built: 10y JGB ~1.6%, Japan ERP ~6%, beta ~1.25 for a high-beta AI-infrastructure cyclical -> cost of equity ~9.1%; net cash so WACC = CoE. 9.0% used, the house JPY industrial reference. Risk is charged ONCE: cyclicality, AI-capex concentration and the tariff dispute are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not as a WACC premium, and WACC is identical across scenarios.
inputs.cash_tax_note: FY2026 effective tax 20.8% (42,565 on pretax 204,613) was flattered by deferred-tax movements; cash tax paid 44,157 = 23% of OP. Japanese statutory ~30.6%, overseas mix lower. Path ramps from 29% (guidance year, includes ~2.5pp NCI leakage) to 31% steady state.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year explicit horizon, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing: non-US cyclical operating company -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Fresh build, no prior DCF. Fujikura is a diversified cable/FPC/harness manufacturer whose Telecommunication Systems segment (55% of FY2026 revenue, ~80% of OP) has become the profit engine of the AI data-center fiber/optical-component build-out: consolidated EBITDA margin went 11.5% (FY2024) -> 16.0% (FY2025) -> 18.1% (FY2026) -> ~26% guided for FY2027 (OP 432bn on 1,755bn, raised three times in 2026). The central judgment in every scenario is how much of the current ~34-37% Telecom segment margin is pricing power in a temporary global fiber shortage versus a durable mix shift. All three scenarios mean-revert the consolidated EBITDA margin; they differ in how far and how fast. The industry (Fujikura, Corning, YOFC, Sumitomo, Prysmian) is adding capacity simultaneously -- Fujikura alone targets 3x fiber/SWR/WTC capacity under a up-to-300bn Japan+US plan -- which is why even the bull case does not hold a 26% consolidated margin in perpetuity. Capex steps up to 4.5-5.5% of revenue for the plan years then settles to 3.5%. Working capital is a manufacturer's (receivables + inventory ~37% of revenue vs payables ~11%): growth consumes ~20% of incremental revenue; contraction releases it. The Jun-2026 'tariff provision' (13,836, the US CBP country-of-origin dispute) is deducted in the equity bridge as a cash claim. Investment securities (56,052 at Jun-2026, mostly listed cross-holdings) are added at book in the bridge with their dividend income stripped from the flows. Real-estate segment (legacy Tokyo sites, ~5bn OP) stays in the operating flows, no separate asset credit. Price is a regular Tokyo close; note the stock has fallen ~46% from its July level and ~63% from the April high (7,933) ahead of this build. The Q2 FY2027 (half year to 30 Sep 2026) results, due in early November 2026, were not in the folder at build time -- the FY2027 guidance used here is the 7 Aug 2026 revision and should be re-checked against that print. House and street bases coincide (SBC = 0), so band_position is null by construction.

bear.narrative: FY2027 lands a little under guidance (H2 project slippage, yen strength, Section 301 and a CBP ruling that goes against the company), then hyperscaler capex enters a digestion phase in 2027-28 just as the industry's capacity additions arrive: a fiber glut of the 2002 kind takes revenue back to ~1.2tn by FY2029 and consolidated EBITDA margin to 11-12% (Telecom back to mid-teens, Electronics loss-making, harness flat). The 300bn plan is partly stranded, so D&A runs above capex for several years. The business survives comfortably (net cash, 57% equity ratio) -- this is an earnings bust, not a solvency case.

base.growth_note: Y1 45% = ~1,714bn against the 7-Aug-2026 guidance of 1,755bn (+48.4%), a small haircut for the H2-weighted phasing, the 160 USD/JPY assumption (2.7bn OP per yen) and Section 301 tariffs. Y2-Y3 slow as the first wave of data-center projects completes; Y4-Y5 a flat-to-down digestion phase as industry capacity (Fujikura 3x, plus Corning/YOFC/Sumitomo) catches demand; Y6+ GDP-plus growth on the enlarged base.
base.margin_note: Y1 25.5% vs ~26.3% implied by guidance (OP 432bn + ~30bn D&A). Reverts to 16.5% by Y7: Telecom at ~55-60% of revenue on a ~20% normal segment margin (its FY2024 level) plus legacy segments at 3-5% gives ~13-14% OP, ~16.5% EBITDA -- structurally above the 8-9% pre-AI era because of mix, well below the FY2027 peak.
base.capex_note: FY2026 cash capex 39bn (3.3%). The Sakura next-gen fiber plant (~45bn) and the up-to-300bn Japan+US 3x-capacity plan lift capex to ~75-100bn/yr for Y1-Y4, then 3.5% of revenue (slightly above 3.0% D&A for 2.5% growth).
base.narrative: AI data-center fiber demand stays strong through FY2027 and FY2028 but pricing normalises from FY2029 as the industry's new capacity lands; Fujikura keeps its share and a richer mix, so mid-cycle margins settle roughly double the pre-boom level rather than at the FY2027 peak.

bull.narrative: The fourth guidance raise comes at Q2; the 3x capacity plan sells out as it lands (multi-fiber SWR/WTC and MT-ferrule components stay supply-constrained into the 2030s), the US fiber subsidiary opens tariff-free domestic supply, and the non-US data-center project pipeline broadens the customer base. Consolidated EBITDA margin holds mid-20s for three years and still settles at 20% -- Telecom at ~28% through pricing discipline and a component-heavy mix -- so FY2036 revenue is ~3.5x FY2026.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: ~80% of operating profit now rides one secular theme (AI data-center capex) whose margin expansion is both extreme (Telecom segment ~20% -> ~37% in two years) and recent, the whole industry is adding capacity into it, and the May-2026 mid-term plan plus the US tariff dispute show management itself does not underwrite the peak. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs two independent things to hold -- hyperscaler capex to keep growing AND pricing to survive an industry-wide capacity tripling. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
